answer: Collateral is slashed jointly when correlated behavioural faults fire inside the same window. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The wharf is the collateral at risk, the quill the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the juniper the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many quill groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the wharf into smaller, individually useless stakes.
